question: Which statement best describes Import Link?
options: The `href` property names the destination, such as `/products`. It should match a real route in the app. A link is a promise that the destination exists, like a sign pointing to a room. Avoid `href="#"` as a placeholder because it jumps unexpectedly and does not communicate a real destination. Use a button when the action changes the current page without navigation. In practice, a missing local route should lead to a deliberate not-found experience, not an empty screen.

Link text should tell people where they will go, even when read outside its paragraph. “Read the setup guide” is clearer than “click here.” This is like labeling a door with the room name instead of “go.” Clear names help screen-reader users scan a list of links and help everyone decide whether the destination matches their task. In practice, make the visible link label understandable when a screen reader lists links alone.

Use a regular `<a>` element for an external website or a file download. The browser then applies familiar behavior, including opening a new tab when requested and showing the destination URL. External navigation is like leaving the building for another address. If a link opens a new tab, tell users when that behavior may surprise them. In practice, use an anchor for another domain even when both sites share a brand.

Import `Link` from `next/link` and render it around readable link text. Next.js can prepare nearby pages and navigate between app routes without requesting a completely new document in many cases. It is like an indoor hallway that avoids leaving and re-entering the building. Links still need to work with a keyboard and have a visible focus indicator. In practice, keep an internal destination in the app route format so navigation stays within the site.
